Gamepad doesn't respond or buttons are wrong

Nothing happens, a stick is dead, or buttons do the wrong thing. Below are the 4 most common causes on FTC robots, ordered from most to least likely, with how to check and fix each one.

Skip the guesswork — run the interactive diagnosisAbout 4 quick questions narrow this list down to your robot's actual problem.

Quick checks first

  • Does the gamepad icon on the Driver Station light up when you press buttons? Top right of the Driver Station screen. Green = recognized and active, orange (SDK 12+) = unknown controller.
  • Is it a Logitech F310 with the green light next to MODE turned on? The small green LED next to the MODE button in the middle of the F310.
  • If you unplug the gamepad and plug it back in with the sticks untouched, does it stop? Stop the OpMode first, then replug, then reassign with START + A.
  • Does telemetry show the code sending non-zero power to it? Print motor.getPower() (and the mode) in your loop.

Common causes and how to fix them

1 Gamepad not assigned or not recognized

The Driver Station needs to know which gamepad is driver 1 vs 2, and some controllers are not supported.

How to fix it 2 min

  1. Press START + A (driver 1) or START + B (driver 2). The gamepad icon on the DS lights up green when it is active.
  2. In SDK 12+, an orange gamepad icon means the controller is not a known FTC gamepad and buttons may be mapped wrong.
  3. Run the "Test Gamepads" utility OpMode to see what each button really reports.
  4. Use a supported gamepad: Logitech F310, Xbox 360, PS4 DualShock 4, PS5 DualSense, Etpark PS4, REV PS4-compatible.
  5. Add a short USB extension that stays plugged into the Driver Station so the port does not wear out.

Sources: FTC Docs · Troubleshooting common issues · FTC Docs · Gamepad best practices

2 Logitech MODE button is on

On the F310, MODE swaps the left stick and D-pad. The green light next to it is lit.

How to fix it 30 sec

  1. Look for the green LED next to MODE on the F310. Press MODE once to turn it off.
  2. Tape over the MODE button so nobody bumps it in a match.

Sources: FTC Docs · Troubleshooting common issues

3 Gamepad zeroed with a stick pushed

The Driver Station sets stick center when the gamepad connects. If a stick was bumped then, the robot thinks you are always pushing.

How to fix it 1 min

  1. Stop the OpMode, unplug the gamepad, and plug it back in with both sticks untouched.
  2. If a gamepad dropped mid-match while a stick was pushed, wiggle the sticks and let them return to center before restarting.
  3. Re-assign the gamepad: START + A for driver 1, START + B for driver 2.

Sources: FTC Docs · Troubleshooting common issues

4 The code never actually powers it

The motor is configured, but the code sets power 0, sets it in the wrong mode, or the button logic never runs.

How to fix it 5 min

  1. Add telemetry that prints the power you are sending and the motor's mode.
  2. With RUN_TO_POSITION, the motor only moves if you set a target, switch to RUN_TO_POSITION, and set power above 0.
  3. Watch for two parts of the code fighting, like one line setting power and another setting 0 later in the same loop.
RUN_TO_POSITION in the right order
arm.setTargetPosition(1120);                      // 1. target first
arm.setMode(DcMotor.RunMode.RUN_TO_POSITION);     // 2. then the mode
arm.setPower(0.6);                                // 3. then power > 0

Sources: GM0 · Common software issues · GM0 · Encoders
